items.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024
items.q: we went on tour in South Africa as The New Brubeck Quartet. That was Dave, Chris on bass and trombone, and Dan

ctx.x: Had Dave played in South Africa?

Yeah. In 1976. And it was just before the cultural boycott had been announced and there was some opposition to it but by — well mainly what this did is we went on tour in South Africa as The New Brubeck Quartet. That was Dave, Chris on bass and trombone, and Dan, and our agent at the time Associated Booking Corporation (ABC) — I never go into this kind of detail with journalists but I suppose for an archival interview it’s good to know that kind of stuff — and parenthetically every imaginable pertinent document…

Cathy Morphet — Shallis was her maiden name. Cathy Morphet from her second husband — first husband. I’m further down the line — M-O-R-P-H-E-T — went on the road as kind of a liaison person but the thing is with the local contacts that she had and on the surface the local contacts were some music people that she knew. She had always been involved with jazz, and kind of less overtly with a kind of liberation organization people who were, you know that was all kind of off-the-record stuff but constantly taking the…

items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That’s when I brought Darius home. I sat him on the grand piano – Howard’s.

ctx.x: [inaudible] a wonderful message from Darius, that he just wrote a note, “Welcome to this beautiful world.”

That’s when I brought Darius home. I sat him on the grand piano – Howard’s. We were living with Howard – grand piano, and played Milhaud for him, so that that would be the first music he heard, I had that note, “Welcome to this beautiful world,” which it’s so amazing for a guy that’s in a wheelchair, in pain every day of his life, dependent on his wife to push into airplanes or into auditoriums. Nothing ever stopped them from seeing
plays and movies and going to restaurants. And she’s so small, and he was so big, but nothing stopped her. She’s still alive, 104, and living in their old apartment in Pigalle.

items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: We have two pianos on stage, nine foot grands. And I’m sitting at the other one

ctx.x: Maybe I can just wrap up and ask about your sons’ careers. They seem to be going well.

Oh yeah. There’s a recording, just came out last week in England with four of our sons and the London Symphony Orchestra. So we’ve got the test pressing upstairs. And I’m pleased with it. It was for my 80th birthday. When I was 70 they brought the four sons, when I was 75, the four sons, 80. They bring them from all over the world, because Darius is in South Africa, and Danny and Matthew are in California. Chris is a mile or so from here. And we have a big party in England on my birthday. So this recording has a…
Wanted to give credit where it’s due, huh?
